Selected problem statement
Helping a person act safely during an impersonation scam
A caller posing as police threatens the user and demands INR 35,000. The user may have exposed banking information.
The user needs calm clarification, relevant account context and a clear sequence of next steps.
Guardian coordinates protective sandbox actions and optional authorized Google follow-up. Financial actions affect synthetic accounts only.

The complete user journey
Support before, during and after the conversation
Before: sign in, retrieve account context, recent synthetic transactions and prior incidents.
During: clarify caller claims, recognize suspicious activity and build a response plan.
Action and confirmation: request dashboard approval, execute each permitted action and verify state.
After: retain incident history, produce a report and track follow-up reminders.

Application architecture
Separate voice, policy and external services
React dashboard: microphone, Agora RTC/RTM connection, incident plan and approval controls.
FastAPI backend: account sessions, tool allowlist, approval gates and per-user SQLite storage.
Agora Conversational AI: speech recognition, managed language model, tool requests and speech pipeline.
Adapters: Murf Falcon output, a separate synthetic bank, and per-user Google OAuth for Gmail and Calendar.
Sources: frontend/src/hooks/useVoice.ts, backend/app/main.py, backend/app/services/voice.py, backend/app/adapters/. Murf runs in the Agora voice pipeline, not as a separate Guardian speech server.
Agora Conversational AI integration
Real-time voice with a backend-controlled lifecycle
The authenticated backend prepares a channel, user ID and time-limited RTC/RTM token.
The browser joins RTC, publishes the microphone, subscribes to remote audio and connects RTM.
The backend configures the saved agent and starts its session. Status and stop endpoints track the lifecycle.
Agent settings use Deepgram Nova-3 ASR and Agora-managed OpenAI gpt-4o-mini. The public HTTPS tool URL reaches Guardian.

Sources: backend/app/services/voice.py (prepare_voice_session, start_voice_session, voice_session_status, stop_voice_session), frontend/src/hooks/useVoice.ts, backend/app/voice_config.py. Agora SDK pin: backend/requirements.txt. Session parameters: 60-second idle timeout, 3,600-second maximum duration. No measured latency claim.
Agora tool calling
Typed proposals meet application policy
Saved-agent function definitions map camelCase Agora tool names to eight registered Guardian tools.
Agora sends authenticated HTTPS POST requests to /api/agent-tools/{name}. Registered accounts have separate tool credentials.
Pydantic validates arguments. The authenticated account selects the permitted storage scope.
Voice confirmation cannot grant approval. Sensitive tools return the pending action until the dashboard authorizes execution.

Sources: backend/app/tools.py (agora_tool_definitions, CONTRACTS, execute), backend/app/api/tools.py, backend/app/database.py (tool_token). Server timeout in tool definitions: 10,000 ms. Voice-triggered end-to-end tool verification remains pending.
Murf AI Falcon TTS integration
Guardian speech uses the Agora Murf pipeline
The saved agent uses MurfTTS with model FALCON and 24 kHz output.
Murf streaming endpoint: wss://global.api.murf.ai/v1/speech/stream-input
The backend holds MURF_API_KEY in an Agora project secret reference. The browser receives the remote audio track.
Default speech is English with Natalie, locale en-US. A profile fixes the voice and locale when the session starts.

Source: backend/app/voice_config.py (build_guardian_agent). Fields: key=secret_ref(secret_name, "murf"), model="FALCON", sample_rate=24000, rate=0, pitch=0. backend/app/services/voice.py updates the secret and saved agent. Credentials never belong in slides or frontend environment variables. Previously user-confirmed speech is evidence, not a new live speech test.

Registered Guardian tools
Eight narrow contracts support the workflow
Context: get_user_context, get_recent_transactions, get_incident_history.
Planning: create_incident persists the situation, assessment, dependency-aware plan and approval requests.
Actions: freeze_demo_card, notify_trusted_contact, schedule_followup expose approved execution outcomes.
Outcome: generate_report produces a downloadable incident summary. Each invocation records audit and tool-log events.

Sources: backend/app/tools.py, backend/app/api/tools.py. Tools do not expose arbitrary SQL, shell or unrestricted HTTP access. freeze_demo_card/notify_trusted_contact read approval and outcome state. The authenticated approval endpoint executes the side effect.
Agentic workflow and actions
A multi-step response to the INR 35,000 scenario
1. Retrieve user context and transactions. Clarify whether the user recognizes the flagged synthetic payment.
2. Create a persistent incident and explain the protective plan. Ask for approval in the dashboard.
3. Approve a sandbox card freeze. Guardian calls the separate bank and reads account state back.
4. With separate approval, send a Google-authorized contact email and create the follow-up series. Read the results and generate a report.

Sources: backend/app/tools.py, backend/app/services/incidents.py, backend/app/services/external.py. At least two coordinated API calls: POST mock-bank /card/freeze then GET /account to verify card_frozen. Gmail and Calendar are real external actions only in Google mode after account connection and approval. They remain pending live acceptance.
Approval, verification and recovery
Success requires evidence from the resulting state
Approvals name the action and expire after 20 minutes. Authenticated sessions and CSRF checks protect decisions.
Sandbox freeze: an idempotency key prevents replay, then a bank snapshot verifies the card state.
Gmail: read-back checks SENT status. Calendar: stable event IDs and read-back verify the approved time.
Partial calendar failures preserve verified events. Ambiguous failures stop automatic resend and remain visible.

Sources: backend/app/services/incidents.py (approve_action), backend/app/services/external.py, backend/app/adapters/bank.py, backend/app/adapters/google.py. Gmail SENT status proves acceptance into the sent mailbox, not recipient delivery. No automatic safe replay of an ambiguous external send.
